newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes may be vulnerable after spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes may be vulnerable after spinoff.

text.p: Great Lakes Chemical Corp could be vulnerable to a takeover bid after it spins off its Octel unit, Salomon Brothers analyst Tim Gerdeman said.

"Following the spin-off, Great Lakes core portfolio becomes more attrcative to strategic buyers that may have previously shown no interest, due to concerns surrounding the tetraethyl lead business," Gerdeman said.
He also noted that Octel, which accounted for 45 percent of Great Lakes operating cash-flow in 1996, could be vulnerable to a buyer in the fuel additives business.
Great Lakes stock sold off heavily after the announcement, partly because it came out during a raft of earnings, but also because of the lack of a major share repurchase.
The company did authorize the repurchase of up to four million shares, but did not commit to a defined program.
The stock lost 5-1/8, or 10 percent, in heavy volume and was trading up 7/16 at 48-7/16 on Friday.
"Given the sharp stock price correction, we would not be surprised if Great Lakes changed it posture and begins to aggressively repurchase shares, if they remain at current levels," Gerdeman said.

Prior to the spin-off, Octel will raise $400 million in debt to purchase Chevron Corp's 10.65 percent stake in the company and make a $300 million special distribution to Great Lakes after the spin-off.
Looking forward, Gerdeman has a preliminary 1998 earnings per share of $2.42 for Great Lakes and $1.53 for Octel, implying a current stock price for Great Lakes of $40.

If Great Lakes uses its $330 million plus cash to repurchase shares at $45 per share, which would increase Salomon's EPS estimate to $2.60, on a multiple of 18 times earnings, a 10 percent premium to its peer group, Gerdeman says he is comfortable with a share price target of $44.
Octel does not have a "pure-play" peer group, but trading on a price earnings ratio of 6-10 times estimated EPS, the share price target range would be $9-$15.

Standard & Poor's on Friday cut its ratings on Great Lakes to single-'A'-plus from double-'A'-minus citing a meaningful deterioration in the overall credit profile as well as uncertainty regarding steps to maintain credit quality. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
